# OmniSpace — Live in the System, Missing in the Work
> **GitHub-first narrative · GICS11 Real Estate · 2026-10-19.** Fictional architecture learning case. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the KM hub. New people, incidents and options are illustrative. Original research, embedded recruiting reference and13HR child pages remain below. Unattended synchronization is unverified.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — Go-live without connected evidence
An invented property-service workflow is live, but teams use spreadsheets and tenant requests remain unresolved. Test, adoption and value records cannot explain the claimed improvement. This is discovery context, not an actual project incident.
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OSP-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Anika Mehra (OSP-P01)** leads the source's global real-estate transformation agenda. Source scope includes property operations, tenant/resident experience, ESG, finance, procurement, workforce and recruiting.
**Revenue, workforce, property counts, HQ, countries, budget and quantified benefits are not supplied.** They remain evidence gaps.
[Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OSP-M05–08)
Property lead **Maya Patel (OSP-P03)** seeks reliable service; tenant lead **Elena Brooks (OSP-P04)** asks what changes for residents; CFO **David Chen (OSP-P02)** challenges unsupported economics.
Compare independent tool/workstream pilots, central suite first and capability-led pilots connected by the source digital thread. Third option provisional.
Source objective is governed, measurable, adoption-focused transformation, not tool implementation alone.
[Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect the Digital Thread (OSP-M09–12)
Source thread: **Strategy → Capability → Process → Requirement → Solution Design → Build → Test → Release → Adoption → Operational KPI → Business Value**.
Architect **Daniel Weber (OSP-P10)** and process lead **Priya Shah (OSP-P11)** connect ownership and evidence. **Sofia Tan (OSP-P05)** asks which identifiers/contracts link the tools.
Source proposes LeanIX, Signavio, Cloud ALM, Tricentis, WalkMe and change tooling. **Reftrack/Revtrack naming is unresolved**. Roles are source proposals, not verified capabilities orconfigured integration.
[Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Fund and Sequence Learning (OSP-M13–16)
Source phases: **Mobilize → Discover → Design → Build and Validate → Deploy → Optimize**. No dates/durations supplied; no invented36-month plan.
Source workstreams cover recruiting, property operations, finance/procurement, ESG and adoption/change. Each needs owner, capability, process, backlog, test, adoption, change and value KPI.
No financial model orvalidated ROI/NPV/payback supplied. Pilot costs, baseline collection and benefit attribution come first.
[Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Delivery, Quality and Adoption One System (OSP-M17–19)
Delivery lead **Ravi Menon (OSP-P12)**, quality lead **Grace Costa (OSP-P13)**, change lead **Ingrid Sørensen (OSP-P14)** and CHRO **Nadia Fernandes (OSP-P06)** review evidence together.
Illustrative pilot uses synthetic property/recruiting workflow data. Test access, exceptions, regression, rollback, role practice, readiness and task quality. No live tenant/system configuration executed.
[Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Verify Business Value (OSP-M20–22)
Process efficiency, architecture simplification, delivery control, quality, adoption, readiness and recruiting metrics are source examples without numeric baselines/targets.
Value-office lead **Thomas van Dijk (OSP-P16)** distinguishes usage, guided-flow completion and go-live from improved task/process/business outcomes.
Source L1fragmented→L5adaptive maturity is conceptual, not an assessed score. Scale, redesign orstop using evidence.
[Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Anika Mehra—CEO; David Chen—CFO; Maya Patel—Property; Elena Brooks—Tenant Experience; Sofia Tan—Digital; Nadia Fernandes—CHRO; Marcus Okoro—Recruiting; Mei Lin—Data/ESG; Omar Haddad—Security; Daniel Weber—EA; Priya Shah—Process; Ravi Menon—Delivery; Grace Costa—Quality; Ingrid Sørensen—Adoption/Change; Amelia Jones—Procurement; Thomas van Dijk—Value.
[Authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve simulations cover discovery, property service, funding, architecture/process, digital thread, quality, adoption, recruiting, ESG, procurement, certification and hypothetical STAR.
Seven blueprints cover Workforce/HR, Tenant/CX, Finance, Procurement, Property/Asset/Service Operations, Business Transformation and Leadership.
**13unique HR child links preserved**; embedded recruiting mention refers to the sameHR02a page. Child bodies unaudited. External media remain planned.
[Scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [13 HR references](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
Original research stays protected. Exact narrative maps to a GitHub baseline; conflicting edits are held. Other canonical changes require deliberate reconciliation; child pages and attachments are not losslessly mirrored.
[Sources/gaps](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Sync protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/11-real-estate/omnispace-real-estate-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)

## 🌟 GICS11. OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. — Business Transformation Case Study **Enterprise Architecture • Process Transformation • SAP Delivery Lifecycle • Digital Adoption • Quality Engineering • Change Management** This is the main transformation case study page for OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. It connects the company’s broader digital transformation agenda with a practical SAP-enabled implementation ecosystem. ## 1. Case study purpose OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. is a fictional global real-estate enterprise modernizing its business, technology, and people systems. The case study shows how a large enterprise can structure a full business transformation using SAP and partner ecosystem tools across: - **Enterprise architecture management** - **Business process transformation** - **Application lifecycle management** - **Digital adoption** - **Quality engineering** - **Change management** - **Recruiting and talent acquisition modernization** - **Implementation governance and value realization** **Transformation objective:** create a governed, measurable, and adoption-focused transformation model that connects strategy, architecture, process, delivery, testing, change, and business value. --- ## 2. Embedded Transformation Case Study The recruiting transformation workstream is part of this larger business transformation program. HR02a. OmniSpace - Architecting Autonomous talent acquisition - Recruiting Transformation Case Study --- ## 3. Transformation scope
**Transformation layer** **Business question** **Primary tools / technologies**
Enterprise architecture What capabilities, applications, data, and technology are required for the target operating model? SAP LeanIX
Business process management How do current processes work, where are the bottlenecks, and what should the future process look like? SAP Signavio
Application lifecycle management How do we manage requirements, design, build, test, deploy, operate, and improve SAP applications? SAP Cloud ALM
Digital adoption How do users learn and adopt the new systems inside their flow of work? WalkMe
Quality engineering How do we automate testing, reduce defects, and protect business-critical processes? Tricentis
Change management How do we manage stakeholder readiness, communication, training, resistance, and adoption? Reftrack and structured change management solutions
Recruiting transformation How do we modernize talent acquisition to support digital real-estate growth? SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting + SmartRecruiters-inspired capabilities
Integration and automation How do systems exchange data and automate end-to-end workflows? SAP Integration Suite, APIs, event-driven integration, automation tools
Analytics and value realization How do leaders track transformation outcomes and business benefits? SAP Analytics Cloud, process mining, KPI dashboards, value realization scorecards
--- ## 4. Transformation narrative OmniSpace’s transformation is not a single system implementation. It is a **business capability redesign** supported by architecture, process intelligence, lifecycle governance, adoption engineering, automated testing, and structured change management. The enterprise wants to become a digitally operated real-estate business where: - Property operations are connected and data-driven - Tenants and residents receive better digital experiences - ESG, asset, lease, and workforce data become trusted decision assets - Recruiting can supply scarce digital skills faster - Business leaders can see transformation progress through measurable KPIs - Technology adoption is managed deliberately, not left to chance **Case study principle:** transformation succeeds when architecture, process, technology delivery, testing, adoption, and change management are managed as one integrated system. --- ## 5. Tool-by-tool utilization framework ### 5.1 SAP LeanIX — Enterprise Architecture Management SAP LeanIX supports the enterprise architecture layer of the transformation.
**Use area** **How OmniSpace uses SAP LeanIX** **Expected output**
Capability mapping Map business capabilities across real estate, HR, finance, procurement, operations, ESG, and technology Business capability map and transformation heatmap
Application portfolio management Identify legacy, duplicate, redundant, and strategically important applications Application rationalization roadmap
Technology risk visibility Track obsolete platforms, integration risks, and unsupported technologies Technology risk dashboard
Transformation planning Connect business capabilities to applications, data, processes, and initiatives Architecture-driven transformation roadmap
SAP landscape transparency Document SAP and non-SAP systems supporting end-to-end business processes Integrated SAP landscape inventory
**LeanIX role:** provide the architectural “map” of what exists today, what must change, and how the target-state business capabilities will be enabled. --- ### 5.2 SAP Signavio — Business Process Management SAP Signavio supports process discovery, process modeling, process analysis, and continuous improvement.
**Use area** **How OmniSpace uses SAP Signavio** **Expected output**
Current-state discovery Capture how processes actually work across regions and business units As-is process models
Process mining / analysis Identify delays, rework, bottlenecks, exceptions, and compliance gaps Process performance insights
Future-state design Model harmonized future processes aligned with SAP best practices To-be process blueprints
Journey and experience mapping Understand user friction for managers, recruiters, property teams, finance users, and operations teams User journey maps and friction-point register
Process governance Define ownership, controls, roles, process KPIs, and continuous improvement loops Process governance framework
**Signavio role:** convert process uncertainty into measurable process intelligence and future-state design. --- ### 5.3 SAP Cloud ALM — Application Lifecycle Management SAP Cloud ALM manages the implementation lifecycle across requirements, design, build, test, deploy, operate, and improve.
**Lifecycle stage** **How OmniSpace uses SAP Cloud ALM** **Expected output**
Discover and prepare Capture scope, implementation tasks, project structure, and SAP Activate alignment Integrated delivery plan
Explore and design Connect requirements to process scope, fit-to-standard outcomes, and solution design Requirement and design traceability
Realize and test Track configuration, development, defects, test plans, and readiness Build and test governance dashboard
Deploy Manage cutover tasks, deployment readiness, release checkpoints, and go-live controls Deployment and cutover control center
Run and optimize Monitor operations, incidents, integrations, performance, and continuous improvement backlog Post-go-live operations and improvement model
**SAP Cloud ALM role:** act as the delivery control tower for SAP transformation execution. --- ### 5.4 WalkMe — Digital Adoption Framework WalkMe supports user adoption by guiding users inside applications during real work.
**Adoption challenge** **WalkMe-enabled response** **Business benefit**
Users do not know what to do in the new system In-app guided walkthroughs and contextual help Lower training burden and faster time-to-productivity
Managers abandon transactions halfway Step-by-step guidance for requisitions, approvals, reviews, and feedback Higher process completion and adoption
Users make repeated errors Smart tips, validation prompts, and guided fields Lower error rates and better data quality
Adoption is hard to measure Usage analytics and adoption dashboards Evidence-based change interventions
**WalkMe role:** move adoption from classroom training into the user’s daily workflow. --- ### 5.5 Tricentis — Quality Engineering Tricentis supports automated testing, regression protection, and quality assurance across business-critical SAP processes.
**Quality need** **Tricentis-enabled capability** **Business value**
Frequent SAP releases Automated regression testing Reduced release risk
Complex end-to-end processes Business-process-based test design Coverage of critical flows across systems
Manual testing overload Test automation and reusable test assets Faster test cycles and lower effort
Defect leakage after go-live Continuous testing and risk-based testing Higher production stability
**Tricentis role:** protect transformation value by making quality engineering continuous, automated, and business-process-led. --- ### 5.6 Revtrack — Change Management Solutions Revtrack is positioned as the change management layer that helps manage stakeholder readiness, communication, training, resistance, adoption, and benefit realization.
**Change need** **Reftrack-enabled response** **Expected output**
Stakeholder alignment Map impacted groups, sponsors, influencers, and decision owners Stakeholder impact and influence map
Change readiness Track readiness by function, geography, process, and user group Readiness dashboard
Training and enablement Coordinate role-based training, adoption activities, and reinforcement Training and enablement tracker
Resistance management Capture objections, adoption blockers, and intervention actions Resistance log and mitigation plan
Benefit realization Track expected benefits against adoption and process outcomes Value realization scorecard
**Revtrack role:** make change management measurable, structured, and linked to adoption outcomes. --- ## 6. Additional tools and technologies for implementation
**Capability area** **Possible tools / technologies** **Purpose**
Integration SAP Integration Suite, APIs, event mesh, middleware Connect SAP and non-SAP systems across recruiting, HR, finance, property, procurement, and operations.
Analytics SAP Analytics Cloud, dashboards, process analytics, data lakehouse Track transformation KPIs, business value, process performance, and executive reporting.
Data governance Master data governance, data catalog, lineage, data quality tools Maintain trusted golden records and controlled reporting.
Security and identity Identity access management, role-based access, privileged access management Secure enterprise systems and enforce segregation of duties.
DevOps and release management Transport management, release orchestration, CI/CD patterns where applicable Control releases and reduce deployment risk.
Collaboration Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Notion Coordinate requirements, decisions, documentation, and stakeholder communication.
Document management SharePoint, Box, Google Drive, Notion knowledge bases Store process designs, architecture decisions, test evidence, and training assets.
AI and automation AI assistants, workflow automation, document intelligence, recommendation engines Accelerate analysis, drafting, support, testing, knowledge search, and operational decision-making.
--- ## 7. Integrated transformation operating model ```plain text Business Strategy ↓ Capability Architecture — SAP LeanIX ↓ Process Intelligence — SAP Signavio ↓ Solution Delivery — SAP Cloud ALM ↓ Quality Engineering — Tricentis ↓ Digital Adoption — WalkMe ↓ Change Management — Reftrack ↓ Operational Analytics and Continuous Improvement ``` **Integration rule:** every initiative should connect to a business capability, a process, a system, a test scenario, an adoption metric, a change plan, and a value KPI. --- ## 8. Example transformation workstreams
**Workstream** **Business focus** **Primary enabling tools**
Recruiting transformation Improve time-to-fill, hiring manager adoption, candidate experience, and recruiting analytics SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting, SmartRecruiters-style capabilities, WalkMe, SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM, Tricentis
Property operations modernization Improve asset maintenance, field operations, work orders, and service responsiveness SAP LeanIX, SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM, IoT platforms, analytics

--- ## 9. Business value scorecard
**Value dimension** **Example KPI** **Measurement source**
Process efficiency Cycle time reduction, rework reduction, automation rate SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM, operational systems
Architecture simplification Application rationalization, technical debt reduction, capability coverage SAP LeanIX
Delivery control Milestone adherence, defect trends, release readiness, scope stability SAP Cloud ALM
Quality Test automation coverage, regression pass rate, defect leakage Tricentis, SAP Cloud ALM
Adoption Active usage, task completion, guided-flow completion, adoption by role WalkMe analytics, process data
Change readiness Stakeholder readiness, training completion, resistance closure rate Reftrack
Recruiting outcomes Time-to-fill, hiring manager adoption, recruiter productivity, candidate drop-off SAP SuccessFactors, SmartRecruiters-style analytics, recruiting dashboards
--- ## 10. Implementation roadmap
**Phase** **Focus** **Key outputs**
Phase 1 — Mobilize Set governance, scope, business outcomes, architecture baseline, and delivery model Transformation charter, stakeholder map, capability baseline, program plan
Phase 2 — Discover Map current capabilities, applications, processes, pain points, risks, and adoption gaps LeanIX inventory, Signavio as-is processes, change impact assessment
Phase 3 — Design Define future-state capabilities, process models, solution architecture, adoption model, and test strategy Target architecture, to-be processes, SAP Cloud ALM backlog, testing blueprint
Phase 4 — Build and validate Configure, integrate, test, automate, prepare adoption journeys, and validate business readiness Configured solution, Tricentis automation suite, WalkMe guidance, readiness dashboard
Phase 5 — Deploy Run cutover, go-live, hypercare, adoption reinforcement, and benefit tracking Go-live control center, hypercare plan, benefit realization baseline
Phase 6 — Optimize Continuously improve processes, architecture, quality, adoption, and business value Continuous improvement backlog, quarterly value review, optimization roadmap
--- ## 11. Publishing-ready summary ## From technology implementation to business transformation OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. demonstrates how large enterprises can move beyond isolated system implementation and build a connected transformation operating model. By combining **SAP LeanIX**, **SAP Signavio**, **SAP Cloud ALM**, **WalkMe**, **Tricentis**, **Reftrack**, and other implementation technologies, the organization can manage transformation from strategy to architecture, process, delivery, quality, adoption, change, and measurable value. ### Key takeaways - **SAP LeanIX** provides the enterprise architecture map. - **SAP Signavio** provides process intelligence and redesign. - **SAP Cloud ALM** provides the SAP delivery lifecycle control tower. - **WalkMe** provides digital adoption inside the flow of work. - **Tricentis** provides automated quality engineering and regression protection. - **Reftrack** provides measurable change management and readiness tracking. - The recruiting transformation page becomes one embedded workstream inside the broader OmniSpace business transformation case study. --- ## 12. Additional enhancement ideas inspired by industrial transformation case studies The current case already explains the SAP-enabled transformation ecosystem. To make it stronger for website publishing and executive storytelling, the following additional points strengthen the case without moving existing content. ### 12.1 Strategic transformation assets
**Strategic asset** **Why it matters** **Transformation use**
Business capability map Creates a common language between business, IT, HR, finance, operations, and leadership Managed through SAP LeanIX as the anchor for scope, prioritization, and roadmap decisions
Process repository Prevents each region or function from redesigning processes differently Managed through SAP Signavio as the source of truth for as-is, to-be, and governed processes
Delivery control tower Gives program leaders visibility into requirements, build, test, defects, cutover, and operations Managed through SAP Cloud ALM for SAP Activate-aligned delivery governance
Adoption intelligence Shows whether users are actually changing behavior after go-live Measured through WalkMe usage analytics and role-based adoption journeys
Automated quality baseline Protects critical business processes from release defects and regression failures Built through Tricentis test automation and risk-based quality engineering
Change readiness record Tracks who is ready, who is resisting, and where leadership intervention is needed Managed through Revtrack / change management tooling and readiness dashboards
--- ### 12.2 Transformation governance model **Governance idea:** create one integrated transformation governance model where architecture, process, delivery, testing, adoption, and change are reviewed together — not as separate project status reports.
**Governance forum** **Primary focus** **Decision rights**
Executive steering committee Business outcomes, investment, risk, and value realization Approve scope, funding, sequencing, and benefit commitments
Architecture review board Capability alignment, application rationalization, data, integration, and technology standards Approve target architecture and major design exceptions
Process council Process standardization, local variation, controls, and process KPIs Approve to-be processes and process ownership model
Delivery control tower Requirements, build, test, defects, cutover, release readiness, and hypercare Approve readiness gates and deployment decisions
Adoption and change council Stakeholder readiness, training, WalkMe adoption data, resistance, and reinforcement Approve adoption interventions and change actions
Value realization office Benefits tracking, KPI movement, and continuous improvement backlog Validate realized value and prioritize optimization actions
--- ### 12.3 Target-state digital thread ```plain text Strategy → Capability → Process → Requirement → Solution Design → Configuration / Development → Test Scenario → Release → User Adoption → Operational KPI → Business Value ``` **Digital thread rule:** every major transformation item should be traceable from business strategy to measurable business value. This gives OmniSpace a stronger executive narrative: the transformation is not simply “implement SAP tools,” but **create traceability from strategy to value**. --- ### 12.4 Risk and control architecture
**Risk area** **Potential issue** **Control response** **Tool support**
Scope risk Transformation expands without clear prioritization Capability-based roadmap and governance gates SAP LeanIX, SAP Cloud ALM
Process risk Regions create too many local variations Global process template with controlled localization SAP Signavio
Delivery risk Requirements, tests, defects, and releases lose traceability Integrated lifecycle governance and readiness gates SAP Cloud ALM
Quality risk Regression defects affect business-critical processes Automated regression suite and risk-based testing Tricentis
Adoption risk Users bypass the new system or revert to spreadsheets In-app guidance, usage analytics, champion network, leadership reinforcement WalkMe, Revtrack
Value risk Project goes live but benefits are not realized Value scorecard, post-go-live optimization backlog, quarterly benefit reviews SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM
--- ### 12.5 Security, compliance, and resilience layer For a website-ready business transformation case study, add a visible security and resilience lens.
**Security / resilience theme** **Case study relevance** **Example control**
Identity and access Large transformation programs create new roles, permissions, and external partner access Role-based access, segregation of duties, privileged access review
Data privacy Recruiting, HR, tenant, supplier, and employee data must be protected across regions Consent, retention, audit trail, and regional privacy controls
Integration security SAP and non-SAP systems exchange sensitive business data API security, encryption, monitoring, and integration governance
Operational resilience Go-live failures can disrupt business-critical processes Cutover rehearsals, rollback plans, hypercare model, incident response
Audit readiness Executives need evidence that transformation decisions and controls are traceable Documented approvals, test evidence, change logs, and process controls
--- ### 12.6 Transformation maturity model
**Maturity level** **Description** **OmniSpace target**
Level 1 — Fragmented Processes, systems, and data are managed locally with limited governance Current-state pain point in several functions
Level 2 — Standardized Core processes and templates are defined, but adoption remains inconsistent Early transformation foundation
Level 3 — Integrated Architecture, process, delivery, testing, and change are connected Minimum target for enterprise rollout
Level 4 — Intelligent Process insights, adoption analytics, automation, and quality engineering continuously improve outcomes Target operating ambition
Level 5 — Adaptive The enterprise senses change, adjusts processes, and reallocates investment dynamically Long-term transformation aspiration
--- ### 12.7 Critical success factors 1. **Business capability first:** do not start with tools; start with the capabilities OmniSpace must strengthen. 2. **Process before configuration:** use SAP Signavio to understand and redesign process before configuring systems. 3. **Traceability from strategy to test:** connect capability, process, requirement, design, test, release, adoption, and KPI. 4. **Adoption by design:** use WalkMe and change analytics before go-live, not after users struggle. 5. **Quality as a continuous discipline:** use Tricentis to protect core business processes across releases. 6. **Change management as data:** track readiness, resistance, training, communication, and benefit realization. 7. **Value realization after go-live:** treat deployment as the start of measurable business improvement, not the end of the project. --- ### 12.8 Stronger positioning statement ## Positioning statement OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. shows how enterprise transformation becomes measurable when SAP LeanIX, SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM, WalkMe, Tricentis, Revtrack, and analytics are connected into one operating model. The result is a transformation system where leaders can see what must change, how processes will improve, how delivery is controlled, how quality is protected, how users adopt, and how value is realized. --- ## 13. Suggested website sections - [ ] Hero banner: “OmniSpace Business Transformation Case Study” - [ ] Transformation ecosystem diagram - [ ] Tool-by-tool capability cards - [ ] Embedded recruiting transformation story - [ ] SAP delivery lifecycle roadmap - [ ] KPI and value realization dashboard - [ ] Transformation governance model - [ ] Strategy-to-value digital thread - [ ] Risk and control architecture - [ ] Security, compliance, and resilience layer - [ ] Change and adoption model - [ ] Quality engineering strategy - [ ] Critical success factors - [ ] Call-to-action: “Design your SAP transformation operating model” --- ## 14. Aligned business transformation case study blueprint ## Alignment purpose This section converts the existing OmniSpace content into a clearer business transformation case study format. It does not replace the current material; it creates a structured storyline that can be used for teaching, consulting, website publishing, or executive presentation. ### 14.1 Executive case narrative OmniSpace Real Estate Ltd. is moving from a fragmented real-estate operating model to a governed, data-driven, adoption-focused enterprise transformation model. The transformation connects business strategy, enterprise architecture, process redesign, SAP-enabled delivery, quality engineering, user adoption, change management, and measurable value realization. **Core transformation statement:** OmniSpace is not only implementing tools; it is building a repeatable transformation operating system where every initiative is traceable from business capability to process, solution, test, adoption, KPI, and business value. ### 14.2 Business problem statement
**Problem area** **Current challenge** **Transformation need**
Fragmented architecture Applications, processes, and data are managed separately across regions and functions. Create a capability-led enterprise architecture view using SAP LeanIX.
Inconsistent processes Local process variations create rework, unclear ownership, and inconsistent user experience. Use SAP Signavio to discover, redesign, govern, and continuously improve processes.
Delivery complexity Requirements, configuration, testing, defects, releases, and operations are difficult to trace. Use SAP Cloud ALM as the delivery control tower across the SAP lifecycle.
Adoption gap Users struggle to follow new processes and often return to old workarounds. Use WalkMe and structured change management to guide users inside the flow of work.
Quality risk Manual testing and complex integrations increase regression and go-live risk. Use Tricentis for automated, business-process-led quality engineering.
Value visibility Transformation benefits are difficult to measure after go-live. Create KPI scorecards, benefit tracking, and continuous optimization loops.
### 14.3 Target transformation operating model ```plain text Business Outcomes ↓ Capability Map — SAP LeanIX ↓ Process Architecture — SAP Signavio ↓ SAP Delivery Lifecycle — SAP Cloud ALM ↓ Automated Quality — Tricentis ↓ In-App Adoption — WalkMe ↓ Change Readiness — Revtrack / Change Management ↓ Analytics, Optimization, and Value Realization ``` **Operating rule:** Every workstream must have a named business owner, target capability, process scope, solution backlog, test coverage, adoption metric, change plan, and value KPI. ### 14.4 Workstream alignment map
**Workstream** **Business outcome** **Architecture / process focus** **Delivery and adoption focus**
Recruiting transformation Faster hiring, better candidate experience, stronger hiring manager adoption Talent acquisition capability, requisition-to-hire process, recruiting analytics SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting, WalkMe guidance, Cloud ALM delivery, Tricentis regression tests
Property operations modernization Improved service responsiveness, maintenance visibility, and asset reliability Property operations capability, work-order process, asset data model Integrated SAP/non-SAP workflows, mobile adoption, operational dashboards
Finance and procurement transformation Standardized spend control, faster procurement cycles, improved compliance Source-to-pay, record-to-report, budget governance, supplier lifecycle SAP Ariba / SAP S/4HANA integration, Cloud ALM backlog, Tricentis testing
